questions.question: How do you manipulate strings in Ruby?
questions.title: String Manipulation in Ruby
questions.direct_answer: Ruby strings have many methods: split (to array), join (array to string), upcase/downcase/capitalize, strip (trim whitespace), sub (first match) and gsub (all matches, with regex), chars (to array of chars), reverse, include?, replace, +, <<. Strings are mutable in older Ruby but frozen by default in 3.0+ for literals; use << or += to build. Common interview moves: split to tokens, gsub with a regex to replace, chars.tally to count, reverse to check a palindrome. Know strings vs symbols: strings are mutable text; symbols are immutable interned labels.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know split/join/gsub/strip/chars/reverse and that strings are text (mutable-ish) vs symbols (immutable labels).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Using sub (first only) when you meant gsub (all), or confusing a string with a symbol.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: split/join/gsub/strip/chars/reverse are the common string methods. sub is first-only; gsub is all (regex). Strings are text; symbols are immutable labels.

sections.title: String manipulation
sections.content:
```ruby
s = 'Hello, World'

s.split(', ')            # ['Hello', 'World']
s.split(', ').join('-') # 'Hello-World'

s.upcase                 # 'HELLO, WORLD'
s.downcase               # 'hello, world'
s.strip                 # '  hi  ' -> 'hi'

s.gsub(/[aeiou]/, '*')   # 'H*ll*, W*rld' (all vowels)
s.sub(/l/, 'L')          # 'HeLlo, World' (FIRST match only)

s.chars                 # ['H','e','l','l','o',',',' ','W','o','r','l','d']
s.chars.tally           # {'H'=>1, 'e'=>1, 'l'=>3, ...}
s.reverse               # 'dlroW ,olleH'

# Palindrome check (ignore case + non-letters):
def palindrome?(s)
  clean = s.downcase.gsub(/[^a-z]/, '')
  clean == clean.reverse
end
```
